Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
620 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes to the forecast. Trends have been towards 
a less impactful system Sunday into Monday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Low pressure moving up the coast will impact the area with 
rain Sunday afternoon into Monday morning. Minor localized coastal
impacts possible due to approaching full moon on Tuesday.

2) Another coastal storm is possible from Wednesday night into
Thanksgiving Day. More widespread coastal flooding is possible 
depending on low track and intensity.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...

A broad area of low pressure off the SE coast is poised to
develop into a more organized surface low pressure late today
and into Sunday. Latest guidance has two distinct areas of low
pressure, a weaker and more widespread low along the coast, and
a more compact, slightly stronger low which moves up the coast
but remains offshore. The offshore area of low pressure
continues to gradually strengthen as it moves north and becomes
the primary low.

As of the 00Z model guidance, all models, including the AI
models, have shifted slightly east, along with the axis of
heaviest rainfall. A few showers may become possible Sunday
morning into the early afternoon, but more widespread rainfall
is expected by Sunday evening and into the overnight hours. 
Ample moisture and lift right ahead of the low pressure may 
result in an area of briefly heavy rainfall somewhere over the 
area, though based on the 00Z guidance, it is more likely for 
the eastern portions of the area. A few thunderstorms are also 
possible given the strong forcing and weak instability, mainly 
for eastern areas.

Despite the most recent trends, there remains inherent
uncertainty in the low track, intensity, and the potential
interactions with an approaching shortwave trough from the west
that may bring the heaviest rainfall back west. Given this
uncertainty, WPC maintains a marginal risk for excessive
rainfall over much of the area with the primary concern being
minor urban, poor drainage, and small stream flooding,
especially given the quick hitting nature of this system. A 
widespread 1-2" of rainfall remains possible, with localized 
higher amounts of up to 3" in the heaviest of rainfall if a more
persistent training band of heavy rain materializes. There are 
also some hints that there may be a sharp cutoff of 
precipitation to the west with some guidance having very little 
rainfall for NYC and points west. While total QPF has trended 
slightly less for western areas in this forecast, have opted not
to be too drastic with changing rainfall amounts at this time given
the aforementioned uncertainty.

Wind impact Sunday night will depend on the track of the sfc 
low. Generally anticipating winds to increase out of the E as 
the low approaches the area with sustained wind 10-15 mph and
gusts upwards of 25-30 mph possible along the coast. There is a
low chance for a brief period of gusts along the coast that may
approach 40-45 mph, but this is a low probability at this time
and would be confined to a small area to the east if it were to
occur.

The coastal flood threat continues to look minimal as high tide
occurs Mon AM after passage of the low center. A few Long 
Island south shore back bays locations may approach or touch 
minor thresholds during that time. 


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Models continue to agree on a potentially large, impactful 
coastal low pressure system developing in the Wednesday to 
Thanksgiving Day timeframe. While impacts at this time remain 
too uncertain to hone in on, this system has the potential to be
more impactful regarding wind and coastal flooding than the 
system moving through on Sunday into Monday. Also worth noting 
is that while most models have some sort of large low pressure 
system, the mid and upper level pattern is complex enough where 
any subtle change can result in large differences in intensity,
track, and timing. At this time, it is something to keep 
monitoring.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
High pressure remains in control through tonight. Low pressure
approaches from the south on Sunday.

VFR through the TAF period. There is a chance for -RA late
Sunday morning. 

Light NE or variable flow this morning will become SE by this
afternoon 5-7 kt. Winds weaken this evening and become light and
variable. NE winds begin increasing Sunday morning. 

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of wind shift to the SE may be off by 1-2 hours. 

.OUTLOOK FOR 12Z Sunday through Wednesday... 

Sunday: VFR in the morning. MVFR conditions develop in the
afternoon with -RA. RA expected at night with MVFR-IFR
conditions. E-NE gusts 20-30 kt, strongest east of NYC terminals.

Monday: MVFR to start, becoming VFR into the afternoon. NW wind
gusts 15-20 kt. 

Tuesday: VFR. 

Wednesday: VFR. MVFR or lower possible at night with chance -RA

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Low pressure moving up the coast will likely produce SCA 
conditions on much of the ocean waters as well as the eastern 
LIS and eastern LI bays Sunday night into Monday. Sheltered 
waters at this time remain just below SCA thresholds, but subtle
changes in the low may increase the SCA potential on the non- 
ocean waters. Depending on low track there is a chance for gales
on the ocean waters and the ern Sound/bays Sunday night. SCA 
conditions likely persist into at least Tuesday on the ocean as
waves will be slow to come down.

Gales are possible on all waters Wed night with the area 
sandwiched between an approaching coastal storm and strong high 
pressure to the north.
